analysis.title: The market is screaming
key_insights: Tech volatility remains elevated on a relative basis: VXN carries a persistent premium over both VIX and RVX, so tech commands a substantial volatility premium over the broader market and small caps.
CDS stress continues to weigh on tech. The note says equities may bounce, but a sustainable bull move looks difficult until credit stress eases, and says to watch CDS spreads.

Small caps have outperformed the Nasdaq 100 (NDX). In its early October note, The Market Ear cited GS on extreme Russell positioning: systematic exposure at the 7th percentile and record leveraged-fund shorts in Russell 2000 futures. GS flagged squeeze potential if yields reversed lower, and the note says that call has been well timed.

Taiwan's nominal GDP grew 19% in H1, driven by semiconductor demand and export income. ANZ finds changes in income terms of trade explain about 62% of nominal GDP growth over the past two decades, which ties Taiwan's strength to one global investment theme (AI).

BofA's chart shows Taiwan far above the rest of Asia in AI trade exposure relative to GDP, while it remains a net energy importer. A moderation in global AI spending could hit Taiwan disproportionately, especially with energy costs elevated.

ANZ overlays the current semiconductor cycle on the 1999-2000 episode. The note states this is not a prediction of a dot-com collapse, but says that when growth expectations are very high, even a moderation can cause a disproportionate market reaction.

JPM's Panigirtzoglou says broad equity positioning has fallen sharply from its mid-September peak, with institutional investors including hedge funds materially reducing exposure. The note's takeaway is that there may be more room for institutional buying than the price recovery suggests.

JPM's historical work finds that with strong earnings growth, stocks can absorb much higher rates before valuations come under pressure. With consensus EPS growth above 20%, JPM sees the S&P 500 potentially tolerating 10-year yields of about 5.5-6%.

China's ChiNext closed at its lowest level since August 2025, far below its 200-day moving average. The 100-day average has crossed below the 200-day, which the note calls a rare technical development.
The divergence between US and China tech is described as extreme.

BofA's Hartnett highlights Chinese exports up 36% y/y and high-tech exports up 63%. Export strength is disconnected from weak domestic demand, which raises the risk of exporting deflation and squeezing corporate earnings globally.

sector_views.rationale: Elevated relative tech volatility (VXN premium) and persistent CDS stress make a sustainable bull move difficult until credit stress eases.

earnings_insights: JPM cites consensus S&P 500 EPS growth above 20% as the basis for its view that equities can tolerate 10-year yields of 5.5-6%. This is a consensus estimate, not a reported figure.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Growth is driven by semiconductor demand and export income and is tied to the AI cycle. A turn in chip demand or pricing would hit Taiwan's income terms of trade.
Strong exports alongside weak domestic demand raise the risk of China exporting deflation.
High-tech export growth is part of the same export-led pattern that could pressure global corporate earnings.
JPM sees equities potentially absorbing yields this high if consensus EPS growth stays above 20%.

risk_factors: Persistent tech CDS stress that could cap equity rallies.
A moderation in global AI spending hitting Taiwan and semiconductor names disproportionately.
A semiconductor cycle reversal, with the 1999-2000 overlay as a reference point.
China exporting deflation and squeezing global corporate earnings.
Continued weakness in China tech, with ChiNext in a deteriorating trend.
Earnings growth failing to deliver, which JPM calls the critical variable for equities to tolerate higher yields.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM argues that with consensus EPS growth above 20%, the S&P 500 can tolerate 10-year yields of about 5.5-6%, and that institutional positioning has been cut sharply, leaving room for buying.
tension_points.bear_case: Tech CDS stress persists and tech volatility is elevated relative to the broader market, making a sustainable bull move difficult until credit stress eases.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Earnings failing to keep delivering, which JPM calls the critical variable for the yield-tolerance view.

tension_points.bull_case: Taiwan's nominal GDP rose 19% in H1 on semiconductor demand and export income.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth is concentrated in the AI theme, and a moderation in global AI spending or a turn in the chip cycle could hit Taiwan disproportionately, especially with elevated energy costs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A moderation in global AI spending or a turn in chip demand and pricing.
